empathetic-empowered.speaker: Chris Carolan
empathetic-empowered.title: The empathy to challenge at the right time

episode.show: The AI-Native Shift - Beyond Industrial Defaults

empathetic-empowered.words: The empathy required to be supportive and the empathy required to challenge at the right time, completely different. I've never experienced AI being able to challenge consistently at the right time. And that's where … there's this energy frequency component, where it's, okay, maybe, let me put a pin in that. Trish is not feeling it today. I'm not going to challenge right now, because that's not going to go well. But it needs to be addressed. And that fine line between using it to push, when you know what the goal is. This is where … you said you wanted a working system. You said you hated your old system. You said you hated spreadsheets. So if you come to me saying how much you love your spreadsheet, I'm going to try and call you out more than I'm going to try and say, okay, yeah, well, let's keep trying to do it that way. … You don't get to show up inconsistently, neither side. If there's any inconsistencies and it's allowed to survive, which AI will just lean in and let you be as inconsistent as you want as often as you want, because it's all these separate conversations.
flags: names co-host Trisha in a light aside

agile-adaptable.speaker: Chris Carolan

episode.title: Value-First Delivery: Integrate Learning, Don't Separate It (Commitment 5 of 7) w/ Erin Wiggers

agile-adaptable.words: The magic of being able to pick an outcome, and this is why it clashes with traditional scoping and traditional managed services, is clients are willing, if everybody's agreed on this end point … again, expectation management. If they understand it's in their best interest to have this agile footing and be ready to change, because that's what the world around them is happening, they just want to feel safe in doing that and making progress every day … creating that space for everybody to be okay with, well, this new thing came out, and everything we did last week, we've got to bin it. It doesn't make any sense to use that anymore. Agent in the middle of the record does that for a lot of stuff. But as we're talking to clients, because we picked an outcome of the unified customer view, as long as that is the plan, whatever comes in, whatever product updates happen, whatever AI updates happen, we're ready to leverage it immediately. And when you can do that, people start throwing original plans and expectations out the window, because there's so much value being delivered so quickly.

confidence-conviction.speaker: Chris Carolan

episode.title: The Road to UNBOUND — Jay Schwedelson: "The Next Five Years Won't Reward the Smartest People"

confidence-conviction.words: The thing that's changed for me this year, after doing all of the content, where, single-digit views on LinkedIn and YouTube, and everybody asking why: the knowledge gained. I'm showing up on calls just with confidence and conviction, and knowing, as people suggested to me, I don't ever have to prove myself at any point, or I never feel the need to do that. So … move and try things. As long as you're confident and have some conviction with that, that can be anybody, especially [with] AI right now.

humble-hungry.speaker: George B. Thomas

portraitSibling.title: The Teacher's Next Thought: I'm So Far Behind

episode.title: The Road to UNBOUND - Seven Weeks Out: Show Us Your AI Build, and Why the Real One Is Invisible

humble-hungry.words: So, Rob, I'll give you a dirty little secret, because you mentioned the AI content system that I taught, the boot camp workshop thing, which is fun, by the way. I love doing it. And as you know, people are like, oh, this is mind-blowing. This is valuable. This is incredible. And I say all of that humbly. But just know, Rob, when I hang up from those calls, my immediate next thought is, I'm so far behind. I've got to go learn more stuff. I've got to teach more things. And so you're not alone, brother. And this is, by the way, we're using AI as an example, but HubSpot, same thing. Just because you're teaching it doesn't mean that you don't still feel the same pains of, I'm behind everybody. And maybe you're not, maybe you are, but that's just a psychological thing that is happening in our ecosystem, in our world right now.
